experiment.steer: S015 §73 performance claim gates; §112 negative science

kernel.shape: two-stage reduction, three dispatches, one or three host syncs

result.what_was_published: ACCELERATOR_ATOMICS.json diagnosed the two-stage reduction's loss as LAUNCH COUNT and reported that collapsing 3 launches to 1 with atomics bought 3.05x at 2^20 and 1.80x at 2^24, calling the diagnosis CONFIRMED.
result.the_defect: execute_reduce called mx.eval once PER LEVEL of the reduction tree. MLX is lazy, so that split what should be one command buffer into three, with a HOST ROUND TRIP between each. The atomic arm had one launch AND one sync; the two-stage arm had three launches AND three syncs. The comparison moved both variables at once and attributed the result to the wrong one.

atomic_vs_lazy_two_stage_LAUNCHES_ISOLAT.reason: an arm failed the 10.0% IQR gate (two_stage_one_eval 10.56%, atomic_one_launch 6.47%) and the margin 6.39% does not overwhelm that noise

lazy_vs_eager_two_stage_SYNCS_ISOLATED.caveat: an arm exceeded the 10.0% IQR gate, but the margin is 12x the worst arm noise, so the direction of the result is not in doubt; the MAGNITUDE carries more uncertainty than a clean measurement would

lazy_two_stage_vs_mlx.reason: an arm failed the 10.0% IQR gate (mlx_sum 6.64%, two_stage_one_eval 10.56%) and the margin 18.22% does not overwhelm that noise

scan_simd_vs_hillis.reason: an arm failed the 10.0% IQR gate (hillis_steele 11.89%, simd_prefix 10.65%) and the margin 6.60% does not overwhelm that noise

scan_simd_vs_mlx.caveat: an arm exceeded the 10.0% IQR gate, but the margin is 8x the worst arm noise, so the direction of the result is not in doubt; the MAGNITUDE carries more uncertainty than a clean measurement would

atomic_vs_lazy_two_stage_LAUNCHES_ISOLAT.reason: margin 1.91% does not clear arm noise 4.66%

result.correction_1_launch_count_is_REFUTED: Holding syncs at one and varying ONLY launch count (atomic 1 dispatch vs two-stage 3 dispatches) gives NO_CLAIM at 2^20 and INDISTINGUISHABLE (1.019x) at 2^24. Collapsing three dispatches into one buys nothing measurable. The published mechanism is wrong.
result.correction_2_the_real_mechanism_is_HOST_: Holding launches at three and varying ONLY the sync count gives 2.30x at 2^20 and 1.28x at 2^24 -- essentially the whole originally-reported effect. The cost was host round trips and command-buffer boundaries, not GPU kernel launches.
result.correction_3_the_recommendation_FLIPS: The atomics receipt named a real tradeoff: atomic adds land in nondeterministic order and are 3.4x less exact. That trade was worth making for a 3x speedup. It is NOT worth making for nothing. With the sync defect fixed the atomic strategy is INDISTINGUISHABLE from exact two-stage, so two_stage is now the strategy to prefer and atomic is retained only as evidence that float atomics work.
result.correction_4_MLX_wins_by_less_than_publi: ACCELERATOR_REDUCTION.json reported MLX winning ~3x. Roughly half of that was our own harness: with one sync, MLX wins 1.75x at 2^24 and the gate returns NO_CLAIM at 2^20 (margin 18% against 10.6% arm noise). MLX is still the qualified winner for reduction, by a smaller margin.
result.how_it_was_found: Not by auditing the reduction. Building the scan required the same recursive shape, the first scan measurement came out implausibly slow, and removing the per-level eval moved it 2.2x -- which immediately implicated every earlier measurement that used the same loop. A defect in a harness is found by writing a SECOND thing that uses it.
result.blast_radius: Bounded and checked: only execute_reduce and the new scan used a multi-level loop. Every other timed path in this program (fusion, gravity-native, GEMM, softmax, attention, the forge) is a single dispatch with a single eval and cannot carry this defect.

claim_boundary: f32 sum reduction and scan, 2^20 and 2^24, one machine. This does NOT say kernel launches are free in general -- the P7 size sweep separately showed small kernels here are launch-bound. It says that at these sizes, on this runtime, three dispatches inside ONE command buffer cost no more than one, while three command buffers cost 1.3-2.3x more than one.

bench.machine: Apple M3 Ultra, 60 GPU cores, 96 GiB (receipts/headless/MACHINE_GENOME.json)
bench.rule: S032 §3 -- if quiescence is unknown the state is UNKNOWN, not quiet
bench.provenance: this receipt was written before quiescence was a benchmark input and recorded none. UNKNOWN is what it measured under, not a claim that the machine was busy
